account: Parent question: are the claimed bounds, z-interval formula, edge-cell results, and methodology correct and adequate? Answer: the mathematics is correct and adequate — every claimed item was verified at synthesis with exact arithmetic — but the audit as executed did not demonstrate this: children 01, 02, and 04 self-reported blocked (no proofs produced), and child 03, the sole evidence producer, misstated the (7,7) solution and raised a spurious alarm against the z-interval formula. Resolved per conflict policy: (i) 3<=x<=8 and all six y-intervals are exactly right and tight, with explicit failure witnesses just outside each endpoint; (ii) the z-interval formula max(y, floor(1/R)+1) <= z <= floor(2/R) is provable from R <= 2/z and 1/z < R, the +1 handles integer 1/R correctly, and w>=z is automatic since 1/w = R - 1/z <= 1/z; (iii) edge cells: (8,8)->(8,8,8,8) and (3,18)->(3,18,18,18) by equality in 1/z+1/w <= 2/y; (7,8)->zero via (13z-56)(13w-56)=3136 with no divisor of 3136 congruent to 9 mod 13; (7,7)->exactly one solution, but it is (7,7,7,14), NOT child 03's (7,7,14,14) — direct substitution gives 2/7+2/14 = 3/7 != 1/2; the dossier's stated 'one solution with w=14' remains correct; (iv) child 03's claim that the z-interval fails at (7,7) is spurious: it rests on the z=14 error, and the true z=7 lies in the correctly computed interval [7,9]; (v) the 3-term analog fully derives by the same method and totals 10 (5+3+1+1). Provenance caveat: all proofs beyond the four edge cells are synthesis-level reconstructions, not child deliverables; the final document must not cite the blocked child packets as proof carriers. The full per-(x,y) table and grand total for the 4-term problem were never audited.
assumptions: R denotes 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y; it is undefined in the dossier (flagged by child 01) and fixed by context.
x <= y <= z <= w is a sorting convention, WLOG for counting unordered quadruples.
All arithmetic is exact rational; no floating point anywhere in the verifications.

claims.statement: 3 <= x <= 8 is proved: 1/2 = sum <= 4/x forces x <= 8; x <= 2 is impossible since 1/x >= 1/2 leaves no positive residual for y,z,w.

For each x the tight y-interval is max(x, floor(2x/(x-2))+1) <= y <= floor(6x/(x-2)), evaluating exactly to the claimed sets [7,18],[5,12],[5,10],[6,9],[7,8],{8}. Endpoint failures witnessed exactly: x=3,y=6 gives residual 0; x=3,y=19 gives R=13/114 > 2/19=12/114; x=4,y=13 gives R=9/52 > 2/13=8/52; x=5,y=11 gives 23/110 > 20/110; x=6,y=10 gives 7/30 > 6/30; x=7,y=9 gives 31/126 > 28/126.

The z-interval formula is proved: with R = 1/2-1/x-1/y > 0 and z <= w, R <= 2/z yields z <= floor(2/R) (inclusive; equality when z=w=2/R integral, as at (8,8)); 1/z < R yields z >= floor(1/R)+1, correct even when 1/R is an integer because the inequality is strict; z >= y gives the max lower bound. w >= z is automatic since 1/w = R-1/z <= 1/z. This discharges blocked child 02's objective.

Edge cells hand-verified: (8,8) uniquely (8,8,8,8) and (3,18) uniquely (3,18,18,18) by equality in 1/z+1/w <= 2/y; (7,8) has zero solutions since (13z-56)(13w-56)=3136=2^6*7^2 and no divisor of 3136 is congruent to 9 mod 13; (7,7) has exactly one solution (7,7,7,14): (3z-14)(3w-14)=196 with pairs (1,196),(4,49),(7,28) giving z=5,6,7, of which only z=7 >= y survives.

Conflict-policy correction: child 03's stated quadruple (7,7,14,14) is refuted by direct substitution (2/7+2/14 = 3/7 != 1/2). The correct unique solution is (7,7,7,14), consistent with the dossier's claimed 'one solution with w=14'.

Child 03's boundary finding that the z-interval fails at (7,7) is spurious: it stems from the z=14 error; with the correct solution, the interval is [max(7, floor(14/3)+1), floor(28/3)] = [7,9] containing z=7, and z=8,9 give non-integer w=56/5 and 126/13. The z-interval formula stands unmodified.

The 3-term analog 1/x+1/y+1/z=1/2 derives fully by the same method and totals 10: x in [3,6]; x=3: (y-6)(z-6)=36 gives 5 solutions; x=4: (y-4)(z-4)=16 gives 3; x=5: (3y-10)(3z-10)=100 gives only (5,5,10) with y>=5, so 1; x=6: (6,6,6), so 1. This validates the bound-and-enumerate methodology on an independent case.

Pitfall checklist for the final proof, each tied to an observed failure mode: (1) enforce x<=y<=z<=w at every stage — factor pairs with z<y (e.g., z=5,6 at (7,7)) must be discarded; (2) apply the z>=y filter via the max() lower bound; (3) use the reduced a/b in (az-b)(aw-b)=b^2, else the congruence and divisor set change; (4) include ALL factor pairs of b^2, including 1*b^2; (5) when 1/R is an integer the strict bound z>1/R requires the +1 (off-by-one risk); (6) floor(2/R) is inclusive — z=w=2/R is allowed, as at (8,8); (7) the z-interval is necessary, not sufficient — integrality via the factor-pair congruence decides existence, and asserting solutions from the interval alone produced child 03's false z=14; (8) the table must cover every feasible (x,y), not a sample.

counterevidence: Children 01, 02, and 04 self-report blocked: no bounds proof, no z-formula proof, and no 3-term derivation were produced by the assigned audit nodes; all such content above is synthesis-level reconstruction, not child evidence.

Child 03 is the only evidence producer and it (a) misstated the (7,7) solution as (7,7,14,14), (b) contradicts itself on the (7,7) z-interval ([8,9] in C003 versus [7,9] in its own counterevidence), and (c) had every claim runtime-downgraded to hypothesis with zero valid citations.
No child audited the full per-(x,y) enumeration table; the grand total for the 4-term problem remains unchecked by any packet.
